notes: Circuit follows the Fritzing diagram: red lead from breadboard A1 to GPIO17 (physical pin 11); resistor from column 1 to column 5 (row e); LED long leg (anode) in column 5, short leg (cathode) in column 6; black lead from A6 to a GND pin (physical pin 20 in the diagram).
The catalogue rpi-4b only lists a GPIO_HEADER port; header pins are named GPIO17 and GND as the task instructions suggest.

The parts list has 3 jumper leads and solder, but the main circuit needs only 2 jumper leads. The third lead is for the optional 3.3V LED test (led3 image) and is not included. Solder is an alternative way to join the LED and resistor, and the breadboard version is used instead.
The resistor value is not stated in the manual, so no value prop is set. The breadboard photo shows a different resistor from the diagram.
Which resistor leg goes where is arbitrary, since the manual says the resistor can go on either LED leg.

The breadboard photo shows the LED and resistor in series with the legs in adjacent columns, consistent with the diagram. The Pi drawn is a Pi 3 B but the matched catalogue part is rpi-4b, which has the same 40-pin header layout.
